rites.name: Tirakanuta
rites.text: Tirakanuta is the concept of binding oaths, the force that held the Pact together when the worlds of Miarlinnys first broke apart. In the Age of the first sovereign it was invoked as the living law that kept groves and growing kingdoms from falling back into the Sundering.

rites.name: Silaenamwen
rites.text: Silaenamwen is a patient, hungering power from beyond the veil of Miarlinnys, whispering through four fallen seers who each carry a fragment of a broken covenant. It promises ruin to those who listen and rewards every surrender with borrowed might that tears at the world's bones. Its influence is felt most strongly when the prophets gather to speak in unison.

rites.name: Valiastium
rites.text: Valiastium is the concept of a branching ending within Miarlinnys, the moment in the Three Futures when a single story splits and the Library must shelve every outcome. It is less a force than a pressure that makes unchosen endings briefly real before they are filed away.

rites.name: Tharnak
rites.text: Tharnak is a concept of the Miarlinnys Arcane Realm, a shape of thought that rises in the Holy Age when flame-lit temples keep the Library's shelves of possible endings. It is held as a rule that a single decisive word can close one branch of the future while leaving the others open.

rites.name: Kraigoth
rites.text: Kraigoth is the concept of branching endings in Miarlinnys, the principle by which the Three Futures diverge and the Library catalogues each outcome as a separate shelf. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall severed old bonds between the peoples of the Arcane Realm, Kraigoth was felt as the pull toward whichever ending the Library had not yet sealed.
